lessons.title: Story Time: A Spring Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss changes described in a spring-themed story.
success_criteria: I can say what changed in the story.
I can name a sign of spring.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss signs of spring children have noticed.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a spring-themed story, modelling discussion of change and growth.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about changes described in the story.
key_questions: What sign of spring is this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of change/growth theme — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap signs of spring in the story.
lessons.home_link: Look for a sign of spring outside.

lessons.title: Fractions Recap: Halves and Quarters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find half and a quarter of shapes and quantities using a spring context.
success_criteria: I can find half of a shape/quantity.
I can find a quarter of a shape/quantity.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding half/quarter using spring-themed objects (e.g. flowers, eggs).
lessons.independent_task: Children find half/quarter of given spring-themed shapes and quantities.
key_questions: What is a quarter of this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record fraction understanding consolidation — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find half of a group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Signs of Spring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of spring weather and nature changes.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of spring.
I can describe how spring feels different from winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of spring (warmer weather, flowers blooming, new leaves, baby animals).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label signs of spring they observe or know.
key_questions: What is different about spring compared to winter?
What signs of spring can you see?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare spring to winter in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Update seasonal observation journal — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Look for signs of spring with your family.

lessons.title: Painting Spring Flowers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to paint a flower observing its structure.
success_criteria: I can paint a flower shape.
I can add colour and detail.
lessons.starter_activity: Look closely at a real or picture flower.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model painting a flower, discussing petals, stem, and leaves.
lessons.independent_task: Children paint their own spring flower from observation.
key_questions: What parts does your flower have?

differentiation.support: Use a simple flower template to paint within
differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail and multiple flower types

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe observational painting skill — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Look closely at a flower at home or outside.

lessons.title: Writing About Spring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about spring using adjectives.
success_criteria: I can use a spring adjective.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about spring using adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about spring.
key_questions: Can you write a sentence about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary and sentence construction — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share spring sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe spring to your family using new adjectives.

lessons.title: Easter Egg Addition and Subtraction
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition and subtraction problems using an Easter egg context.
success_criteria: I can add Easter eggs together.
I can subtract Easter eggs.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving addition/subtraction problems using an Easter egg hunt context.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve Easter-themed addition and subtraction problems using counters.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record mixed operation fluency — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Practise adding and subtracting with any small objects.

lessons.title: Parts of a Plant
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the basic parts of a plant.
success_criteria: I can name 4 parts of a plant.
I can label a plant diagram.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real plant and discuss its parts.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce plant parts (root, stem, leaf, flower) and their basic functions.
lessons.independent_task: Children label a plant diagram with the correct parts.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the function of each part

lessons.assessment_notes: Note plant structure knowledge — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Look at a plant at home and name its parts.

lessons.title: Easter Egg Decorating
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to decorate an egg shape using pattern and colour.
success_criteria: I can create a pattern on my egg.
I can use colour purposefully.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of decorated eggs from different cultures.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model decorating a paper egg template with pattern and colour.
lessons.independent_task: Children decorate their own paper egg using pattern and colour.
key_questions: Why did you choose these colours?

differentiation.support: Use simple repeating pattern with adult support
differentiation.greater_depth: Create a complex original pattern design

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and colour choice — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Decorate an egg shape or real egg at home if possible.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Spring Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read spring-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read spring words.
I can read a sentence about spring.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending spring-themed words (e.g. 'grow', 'seed', 'nest').
lessons.independent_task: Children read spring-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading spring words over the week.

lessons.title: Doubling: How Many Eggs in Two Baskets?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to double numbers to 10.
success_criteria: I can double a small number.
I can write the doubling number sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model doubling numbers using two equal 'baskets' of Easter eggs.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise doubling numbers to 10 using counters, recording number sentences.
key_questions: Can you show me with counters?

differentiation.greater_depth: Double numbers to 10+ and explain the pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Record doubling fluency, an early multiplication concept — evidence for MATHS.N1/N3.

lessons.title: What Do Plants Need to Grow?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what plants need to grow.
success_criteria: I can name what plants need.
I can say why each is important.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children think plants need.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss plant needs (water, sunlight, air, soil/nutrients) and their importance.
lessons.independent_task: Children plant a seed and predict what will help it grow, recording their plan for care.
key_questions: What does your seed need to grow?
What will happen if it doesn't get water?

differentiation.support: Adult supports planting and simple recording
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for each plant need

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plant needs, beginning an ongoing observation — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Help water a plant at home.

lessons.title: Talking About Easter Traditions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to talk about a tradition or celebration they take part in.
success_criteria: I can talk about a tradition I know.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss Easter or spring traditions/celebrations children may know about.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss respectfully that different families celebrate different traditions in spring.
lessons.independent_task: Children share a tradition or celebration they take part in with a small group.

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and cultural awareness — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of traditions shared.
lessons.home_link: Talk more about your family's traditions.

lessons.title: Shape Patterns: Easter Bunting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to continue and create a repeating shape pattern.
success_criteria: I can continue a repeating pattern.
I can create my own pattern.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model continuing and creating a repeating shape pattern for bunting (e.g. triangle, square, triangle, square).
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own repeating pattern bunting using shapes.
key_questions: What comes next in your pattern?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a more complex ABC or ABB pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Record pattern-making skill — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Display pattern bunting around the classroom.
lessons.home_link: Make a repeating pattern with any objects at home.

lessons.title: Life Cycle: Chick and Egg
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence the life cycle of a chicken.
success_criteria: I can order the life cycle stages.
I can name each stage.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the chicken life cycle (egg, chick, chicken, laying eggs) using a diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence and label life cycle picture cards.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence and explain all stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note life cycle sequencing understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the chicken life cycle sequence.
lessons.home_link: Look up another animal's life cycle together.

lessons.title: Spring and Easter Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about spring and Easter.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's spring and Easter learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about spring, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What is a sign of spring?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on spring facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Fractions, Doubling, Pattern
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fractions, doubling and pattern skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can find half/quarter.
I can double a number.
I can continue a pattern.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of fractions, doubling, and pattern-making.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 25 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N4/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising doubling over the weekend.

lessons.title: Spring Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about spring, plants and life cycles.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of spring.
I can name a plant need or a life cycle stage.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering spring signs, plant parts/needs, and the chicken life cycle.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Spring is Here' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about spring?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note seasonal and plant understanding progress — evidence for SCI.PLA/SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about spring with your family.

lessons.title: Spring Class Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute art pieces to a collaborative spring display.
success_criteria: I can add my art piece to the display.
I can talk about my contribution.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art created this week (flowers, decorated eggs, bunting).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss arranging individual pieces into a collaborative spring display.
lessons.independent_task: Children help arrange their spring art into a large collaborative display.
key_questions: What does it add to the display?

differentiation.greater_depth: Suggest arrangement ideas for the whole display

lessons.assessment_notes: Note collaborative and reflective art skills across the topic — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class admiration of the finished spring display.
lessons.home_link: Describe the class spring display to your family.
